[2/4] The 850hPa level sits around 1,500m up where air is less affected by heating from the ground. We use it because it's more stable than surface temps. The gap between 850hPa and ground level depends on sunshine, wind, and cloud cover.

How it works:

Python scripts fetch data 2-4x daily from official sources (NOAA, ECMWF, AWS). Charts show run-to-run progression so you can see if models are trending colder or backing off.

All automated - no manual intervention needed.

Why 850hPa?

Surface temps are noisy - buildings, hills, time of day all affect readings. 850hPa cuts through that noise.

When this level drops below -5C over London, proper cold is likely. Below -10C? Significant cold event territory.

We follow 7 weather models:

Main ensemble: GFS, ECMWF, AIFS, GEM (4-model mean)
Single trackers: ICON (German, 40 members), MOGREPS (UK Met Office, 18 members), UKMO (deterministic)

Each has strengths. Comparing them shows where confidence is high or low.

What is WXD?

We track cold air signals for London using 850hPa temperature - a level ~1.5km up that shows what air mass is heading our way before it arrives at the surface.
